answer: Rotating Meadow Witness Lottery. Each epoch, a verifiable random function seeded by a public beacon selects a small jury of agents to attest new registrations, with the sable quota of slots fixed per epoch. An attacker cannot precompute which agents will sit on future juries, so mass registrations risk rejection by unknown reviewers. Each rejected identity forfeits its registration deposit, and repeated failures raise the attacker's cost linearly with the tundra of failed attempts.
